issues.legal_issue: A municipal demolition notice served by affixation is invalid when the statutory procedure for service is not proved to have been followed.
material_facts: The municipality affixed the notices to the properties rather than serving them personally.
Even accepting the municipality’s claim that the recipients refused service, it produced no affidavit from the serving officer or other proof of the attempts to serve the notices.
The recipients’ production of the notices and acknowledgement that they had been affixed did not establish compliance with the required service procedure.
issues.conclusion: The notices were not served in accordance with law, and the demolition action taken pursuant to them was illegal.
issues.legal_principle: Section 239(1) of the Jammu and Kashmir Municipal Act required service in the manner provided for serving summons under the Code of Civil Procedure, so far as applicable. Affixation following alleged refusal did not dispense with proof of the service attempts required by that procedure, including an affidavit or other appropriate proof from the serving officer.

predicates.municipal_demolition_challenge: A person challenged a municipality’s action to demolish a structure under a notice concerning its condition.
predicates.notice_affixed_to_property: The municipality affixed the notice to the property instead of completing personal service.
predicates.service_attempts_unproved: The municipality did not prove the attempts to serve the notice in the prescribed manner.

issues.definition: When a municipal demolition is challenged, affixing the notice without proving the prescribed service attempts results in the demolition action being illegal for invalid service.

issues.legal_issue: A demolition notice that allows an unreasonably short time to comply does not satisfy the requirement to specify a reasonable time.
material_facts: The notices gave the recipients only 24 hours to dismantle the structures.
The recipients were carrying on business in the buildings and structures and needed time to deal with their goods and business equipment.
The notices required demolition without allowing time for repairs, although the statute contemplated requiring either removal or repairs.
The municipality had not previously formed an opinion that the structures were so dangerous or dilapidated that they should be demolished.
issues.conclusion: The time allowed was unreasonable and did not comply with the statutory requirement; the demolition action was illegal.
issues.legal_principle: Section 238 of the Jammu and Kashmir Municipal Act required a reasonable time to be specified when a notice required an act for which the Act fixed no time. Section 129 contemplated requiring removal of a dangerous structure or repairs necessary for public safety. In the circumstances, 24 hours to demolish structures used for business, without an opportunity to repair, was not reasonable and left no effective opportunity to comply or pursue an appeal or revision.

rule.if: municipal_demolition_challenge and notice_allowed_only_brief_compliance_time and notice_required_demolition_without_repair_option and structure_used_for_business and no_prior_danger_assessment

predicates.municipal_demolition_challenge: A person challenged a municipality’s action to demolish a structure under a notice concerning its condition.
predicates.notice_allowed_only_brief_compliance_tim: The municipality allowed only a very short time for the recipient to comply with its notice.
predicates.notice_required_demolition_without_repai: The notice required demolition without giving the recipient an opportunity to make repairs.
predicates.structure_used_for_business: The recipient was carrying on business in the structure and needed time to deal with business property there.
predicates.no_prior_danger_assessment: Before issuing the notice, municipal officers had not formed the view that the structure was so dangerous that it should be demolished.

issues.definition: When a challenged municipal demolition notice allows only a very short time, requires demolition without a repair option, concerns a structure used for business, and follows no prior assessment warranting demolition, the demolition action is illegal for unreasonable notice time.

issues.legal_issue: Findings and observations of a High Court that the Supreme Court does not decide are not binding in later proceedings when the Supreme Court upholds the result on a separate ground.
material_facts: The High Court made findings and observations about matters including alleged collusion, the resumption of the properties, and other proceedings.
The Supreme Court found it unnecessary to determine those matters and upheld the High Court’s orders on the grounds concerning service of the municipal notices and the time allowed for compliance.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s findings and observations on matters not decided by the Supreme Court were not binding in proceedings that might later be initiated or continued by either side.
issues.legal_principle: The Court did not decide the collateral issues addressed by the High Court and expressly stated that the High Court’s observations and conclusions on those issues would not bind later proceedings. No earlier case or statutory provision was relied on for this point.

predicates.appeal_from_writ_judgment: A party appealed from a judgment granting relief in a writ proceeding.
predicates.higher_court_upheld_result_on_separate_g: The higher court upheld the result on a ground separate from the other findings made below.
predicates.higher_court_did_not_decide_other_findin: The higher court expressly left the other findings and observations undecided.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a writ judgment is resolved on a separate ground and the higher court leaves other findings undecided, those findings do not bind later proceedings.
